Behavioral strategies—like burrow depth adjustment and soil pile arrangement—augment these physiological adaptations. Evolution has produced a mammal finely tuned to maintain homeostasis underground while avoiding excessive energy expenditure. The integration of anatomy, behavior, and physiology allows aardvarks to thrive in habitats that might seem hostile to other mammals.
